value.text:
National Southwestern Associated University (國立西南聯合大學), commonly called Lianda, was a national public university operating in Kunming, Yunnan, China, from 1938 until 1946. It was a wartime association of National Peking University, National Tsinghua University and National Nankai University. Its recorded motto was 剛毅堅卓. The institution is historical rather than a currently operating university.

The university emerged during the Second Sino-Japanese War. The three northern universities first formed Changsha Temporary University in Hunan in 1937. After Japanese forces bombed Changsha in February 1938, members of the university community traveled west to Kunming. The institution's recorded active period began on 2 April 1938 and ended on 4 May 1946. Following the war, most of its community returned to university campuses in Beijing and Tianjin. A remaining educational institution in Kunming became National Kunming Normal University and subsequently Yunnan Normal University; this should not be equated with a continuing National Southwestern Associated University.

The wartime curriculum included a compulsory General History of China course under national education policy. The historian Ch'ien Mu taught at Lianda and wrote an Outline of National History. Accounts of the university also identify physicists Yang Chen-Ning and Tsung-Dao Lee among its alumni. These descriptions reflect the historical institution and do not establish present-day enrollment, finances, or campus boundaries.

Its precise historical site location is not settled by the supplied references: Wikidata provides an institution-level point at 25.05577°N, 102.69757°E, whereas the Wikipedia infobox lists 25.05916°N, 102.69497°E. These different positions should not be read as independently verified coordinates for an identifiable campus or headquarters.
